prompt:
Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Every category has a bidirectional nature. For example:

One person's sensitivity to the Care/Harm foundation may lead them to support high levels of immigration from poorer nations, to reduce the suffering of those who migrate. Whereas another person's sensitivity to the very same foundation may lead them to oppose those levels, because they believe it could lead to people they care about being harmed.

TEXT_C:
The BNP’s 2010 manifesto casts itself as a defence of democracy, freedom, security and identity. It argues Britain faces an existential crisis from mass immigration, EU rule, multicultural “social engineering,” and Islamism, and pledges to put indigenous Britons first.

- Defence and foreign policy: End the wars in Afghanistan and Iraq, oppose war with Iran, withdraw troops from Germany, renegotiate NATO to ensure independence, raise defence spending, and introduce a compulsory one‑year community service scheme. Adopt a neutral, interests‑first foreign policy, cease interference in the Middle East, and end foreign aid, reallocating funds to domestic needs.

- Immigration: Declare Britain a non‑immigration country; halt all further immigration; deport illegal immigrants and foreign criminals; review post‑1997 citizenship grants; expand voluntary resettlement; restore sovereign border control; and repeal the Race Relations Act and equalities bodies the BNP says enforce multiculturalism, while recognising law‑abiding settled minorities’ rights under a guaranteed British majority.

- EU: Immediate withdrawal to restore sovereignty, lawmaking and courts; end UK payments and EU regulation; rebuild global trade, especially with the Commonwealth.

- Counter‑jihad: Assert Islam is incompatible with secular democracy; ban the burka, ritual slaughter, and new mosques; stop immigration from Muslim countries; deport radical preachers and adherents; and address terrorism by ending mass immigration and adopting a neutral Middle East stance.

- Welfare and civil liberties: “Renationalise” welfare for Britons and contributors only; make the NHS serve British people, end “health tourism,” prioritise British staff, and cut bureaucracy; replace welfare with workfare; repeal ID cards, the Human Rights Act and ECHR jurisdiction; repeal laws restricting speech on race and religion; and reassert parliamentary sovereignty over courts.

- Constitution, media, culture: Devolve to revived counties; create an English parliament and a pan‑British parliament (inviting Ireland); reform the Lords with non‑party experts; introduce citizens’ initiative referenda; tighten postal voting and campaign rules; hold media criminally liable for knowing falsehoods and guarantee rights of reply; promote British history, traditions and saints’ days; protect pubs; and resist “alien” cultural influences.

- Crime: Remove political correctness from policing; restore deterrence with corporal punishment and capital punishment for specified crimes; strengthen householders’ self‑defence; impose hard labour, build a remote penal station for the most dangerous offenders, and ensure full sentences are served.

- Education: Restore traditional curricula, phonics, streaming, grammar schools, and competition; reinstate O‑ and A‑levels; prioritise STEM and vocational skills; free university for those completing community service.

- Transport and infrastructure: Reverse rail privatisation, invest in high‑speed maglev, reduce fuel taxes, charge foreign trucks, ease congestion by limiting immigration, and back new transport technologies.

- Agriculture, fisheries, energy: Support family farms; ban GM crops and non‑stunned slaughter; restore the 200‑mile exclusion zone; prioritise wave, hydrogen and especially nuclear and clean coal; oppose wind turbines and “carbon” levies; keep strategic energy in British hands.

- Housing: Empower councils to build for British citizens with local‑connection tests; abolish quangos; create an infrastructure bank; ease pressure by reversing immigration.

- Economy and industry: Cut spending on “global warming” schemes, immigration/asylum, EU, foreign aid, foreign wars, and quangos; raise the personal allowance to £12,500, restore a married allowance, lift IHT to £1m; curb multinationals’ tax avoidance and offshoring; vet foreign takeovers in the national interest; separate retail and investment banking; oppose privatising natural monopolies; deregulate SMEs; use selective tariffs against unfair imports; build local credit unions and explore local currencies.

- Pensions and IT: Raise the state pension to £150/week and link to earnings; limit reliefs and tighten eligibility to Britons/contributors; invest in technology universities; protect UK IT jobs; nationalise telecoms infrastructure to deliver universal 100 Mbps; strengthen data rights.

Conclusion: Democracy and freedoms are portrayed as imperilled by the EU and mass immigration; the BNP promises national renewal that puts British interests, security and identity first.

TEXT_D:
Change that Works for You — Building a Fairer Britain (Liberal Democrat Manifesto 2010)

Core purpose: hard‑wire fairness into national life by redistributing power — economic, social, political and financial — away from vested interests and towards citizens. After decades of red–blue, blue–red governments, the Liberal Democrats offer fundamental reform built around four priorities:

1) Fair taxes that put money back in your pocket
- Raise the personal allowance to £10,000, a £700 tax cut for most workers; 3.6m low earners and pensioners lifted out of income tax.
- Paid for by: taxing capital gains at income rates; restricting pension tax relief to the basic rate; a 1% Mansion Tax on property value above £2m; replacing Air Passenger Duty with a fairer per‑plane duty (higher for non‑lifeline domestic flights); robust anti‑avoidance and anti‑evasion action; reform of non‑dom status.
- Credible deficit reduction: over £15bn identified savings (e.g., scrap ID cards/biometric passports/ContactPoint; banking levy; cap public‑sector pay rises at £400 for two years; prison reform; reduce quangos; cancel Eurofighter Tranche 3B). No like‑for‑like Trident replacement; Council on Financial Stability to guide the pace of cuts.

2) A fair chance for every child
- £2.5bn Pupil Premium to cut class sizes and fund one‑to‑one tuition for disadvantaged pupils; earlier SEN assessment and better teacher training.
- Free schools to innovate: an Education Freedom Act; independent Educational Standards Authority; a slimmer core curriculum; reform league tables.
- Transform 14–19 pathways: a General Diploma to combine academic and vocational learning; FE parity; right to study at college from 14.
- Scrap unfair university tuition fees, phased over six years (final‑year fees ended immediately); targeted national bursaries.

3) A fair future: jobs and green growth
- Break up the banks, separate retail from investment, reform bonuses, and create Local Enterprise Funds and Regional Stock Exchanges.
- A UK Infrastructure Bank to crowd in private finance for clean energy and transport.
- One‑year green stimulus to create 100,000 jobs: refurbish shipyards for offshore wind; £400 Eco Cash‑Back; insulate public buildings; bring 250,000 empty homes into use; bus scrappage; major youth work‑experience offer.
- Climate leadership: zero‑carbon Britain by 2050; 40% clean electricity by 2020 (prioritising marine/offshore); home insulation up to £10,000 per home; no new coal without top‑tier CCS; reject new nuclear in favour of cheaper conservation/renewables; build a European Supergrid.
- Transport fairness: shift funding from roads to rail; cut regulated rail fares 1% below inflation annually; regulate buses locally; cancel Heathrow R3; per‑plane duty; plan for fair, revenue‑neutral road pricing later.

4) A fair deal by cleaning up politics and restoring liberties
- End safe seats with fair votes (STV) and cut 150 MPs; fixed‑term parliaments; a fully elected, smaller second chamber; a written constitution via a citizens’ convention.
- Cleaner politics: recall corrupt MPs; cap donations at £10,000; statutory lobbyist register; all candidates and parliamentarians tax‑resident in the UK.
- Freedom Bill: roll back the surveillance state; regulate CCTV; protect trial by jury and free speech; end blanket retention of innocent people’s DNA; scrap ID cards; stop unfair US extraditions.

Public services and communities built on fairness
- NHS: cut waste, not care; protect frontline (cancer, mental health, maternity, dementia); integrate health and social care; prevention first; patient entitlements over targets; elected Local Health Boards; GP choice and email access.
- Families: shared parental leave; flexible working for all; end child detention in immigration; stronger youth services; equal minimum wage from 16; carers’ respite.
- Older people: restore the earnings link (triple lock: earnings, prices or 2.5%); scrap compulsory retirement ages; long‑term plan for a Citizen’s Pension.
- Crime: 3,000 more police funded by scrapping ID cards; empower elected police authorities; target what works, including restorative justice; presumption against short prison sentences; evidence‑based drugs policy.
- Immigration: firm and fair — reinstate exit checks; National Border Force; regional points system; enforce against rogue employers; earned citizenship for long‑settled families pre‑2010; humane, independent asylum system with right to work.
- Pro‑Europe, internationalist and principled abroad: lead EU climate ambition and financial reform; aid at 0.7% of GNI by 2013; defence review; fair pay/housing for forces; no like‑for‑like Trident; uphold human rights, end complicity in torture; two‑state solution and end Gaza blockade.

If you want real, lasting change that works for you, choose fairness: choose the Liberal Democrats.
